messages:
alex: FYI we saw an eu-west routing flap around 18:34 UTC that auto-shifted most traffic to us-east. App metrics spiked 5xx and redis queue lag increased. Not sure DNS steering finished.
ops-bot: Automatic region failover executed: set traffic_weight eu-west=0, us-east=100. Health checks started 18:34:12. Rolling back disabled.
sam: Seeing a mixed picture from public DNS checks — some resolvers still returning eu-west candidate CNAME after our change.
sam: dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example.com
sam: ; -> 198.51.100.23  (eu-west edge)
sam: ; -> 203.0.113.45  (us-east edge)
maria: That smells like stale cache at some ISP edges. TTL was 300s on the record before failover; we lowered to 60s as part of the playbook but a bunch of resolvers appear to ignore the new low TTL and honored the original longer one.
jordan: Confirmed with tcpdump on an affected node — inbound traffic from certain ASN ranges still heads to eu-west IPs. Edge caches (CDN) reported 304s left on cached mapping.
kevin: Quick note: us-east GPU pool is hitting 92% pod slot utilization after the shift. If traffic stays like this we need to either enable burst capacity (reserved nodes) or scale up dedicated nodes — cost estimate ~ $30/hr per extra GPU node.
lia: Can we do incremental routing via the global LB instead of relying on public DNS? BGP/anycast/GLB reroutes got us faster control in the last China region incident.
alex: Good point. For this failover we used DNS steering + edge CNAMEs; global LB failover would have been immediate. But we don't have GLB enabled for that customer segment.
sam: Recommending these immediate mitigations:
- purge CDN mapping for affected CNAMEs (in progress)
- announce temporary us-east-only LB via BGP (ops infra)
- spin one extra GPU node (+1) in us-east and enable burst pool
- reach out to top 5 ISPs with stale mappings
maria: Purge command run: curl -X POST https://cdn-admin/purge -d '{"cname":"api.redwood.example.com"}' && sleep 2 && curl -X GET https://cdn-admin/status
maria: CDN responded with purge accepted, but some PoPs show queued state.
jordan: For diagnostics, run: dig +trace api.redwood.example.com; you'll see which NS chain is still serving old IPs. Also check negative caching with TTL in SOA.
kevin: Cost note: spinning +1 dGPU node and enabling burst autoscale estimated at $180 for next 6 hours. Approve? cc: @ops-biz
alex: Approve temporary spend given customer impact. Please include exact ETA for node readiness.
lia: Node spawn started 18:35:40, expected ready 18:40 UTC. BGP announcement scheduled 18:38 UTC.
sam: Follow-up: update runbook lines on TTL strategy. Current playbook says drop to 30s during failover; we should change to a two-step approach because many resolvers ignore <300s: (1) pre-failover set 600 -> 60 for 10m if possible, (2) right before cut set 60, (3) after stability ramp up to 600. Also add GLB as fallback in runbook.
maria: Adding item: pre-warm failover IPs in CDN/edge so cache TTLs refresh quickly.
alex: Post-incident actions: 1) Runbook TTL wording update, 2) Add GLB enablement checklist for enterprise accounts, 3) Automate CDN purge as part of failover playbook, 4) Investigate root cause of eu-west routing flap and whether our health checks gave noisy signals.
ops-bot: Incident tag: region-failover-1812345678. Actions created: A-357 (runbook TTL), A-358 (GLB checklist), A-359 (billing window for burst nodes). Assigned to maria/sam/kevin.
kevin: Will keep an eye on GPU utilization and scale down when below 60% for 15m.
alex: Great. Let's aim to close the loop in the postmortem with clear TTL guidance and a cost/tradeoff appendix. Thanks team :thumbsup:
